content_units: Best-Fit Lisbon Apartments for September 2026

For your priorities,   Campo de Ourique (B)   is the best overall fit, followed by   Arroios (A)  . The main tradeoff is simple: B is the most balanced for quiet + light + livability, while A wins on commute but gives up some quiet and comfort.
Ranked Options
Rank   Option   Area   Rent   Fit for Priorities   Key Tradeoffs
1     B     Campo de Ourique     €1,680     Best overall match   Near top of budget; commute close to your limit
2     A     Arroios     €1,550     Strong value and fast commute   Medium street noise; no elevator; smaller space
3     C     Benfica     €1,300     Best space-for-money   Commute exceeds your 35-minute limit; only moderate light
4     D     Areeiro     €1,720     Excellent location and commute   Over budget, even before utilities/moving costs
Option 1:   Campo de Ourique (B)     Best balance of quiet, bright, and workable home feel     Quiet street + bright + balcony

-   Why it ranks first:   It meets your budget cap, stays within the commute target, and aligns especially well with your lifestyle priorities: quiet street, good natural light, and a better day-to-day feel for remote work.
-   Remote work fit:   58 m² is workable for a couple in a 1BR, and the balcony adds breathing room that often matters when both people spend more time at home.
-   Main tradeoff:   At   34 minutes  , it is just inside your commute limit, so there is less buffer for slower transit days.
Option 2:   Arroios (A)     Best commute-to-price ratio     22-minute commute
-   Why it ranks second:   Strong all-around value: comfortably under budget, bright, and very good commute time.
-   Remote work fit:   52 m² is usable for a couple, but more compact than B and may feel tighter if both need dedicated work setups.
-   Main tradeoffs:     Medium street noise   directly conflicts with your quiet-street priority, and   3rd floor with no elevator   can become annoying for groceries, moves, and daily life.
Option 3:   Benfica (C)     Best budget and space, but misses a key constraint     75 m² / 2BR
-   Why it ranks third:   On pure value, this is excellent: lowest rent and the only option with clear extra room for two people working from home.
-   Remote work fit:   Probably the best interior layout potential because a second bedroom can become a proper office.
-   Main tradeoffs:   The   41-minute commute   misses your stated maximum, which is a major constraint, and   moderate light   is weaker than your preferred setup.
Option 4:   Areeiro (D)     Great location, but budget miss pushes it down     18-minute commute
-   Why it ranks fourth:   If budget were slightly higher, this would be very competitive: bright, quiet, and excellent commute.
-   Remote work fit:   Solid, though at 50 m² it is not especially spacious.
-   Main tradeoff:     €1,720   is over your cap before factoring in utilities, internet, deposits, and setup costs, so it fails a core requirement.
Priority-by-Priority Verdict
-   Budget up to €1,700:   B, A, and C qualify; D does not.
-   1–2 bedrooms:   All options qualify.
-   Under 35 minutes to Saldanha:   B, A, and D qualify; C does not.
-   Quiet street:   B and D are strongest; C is also good; A is weaker.
-   Natural light:   A, B, and D are strong; C is weaker.
-   Remote work space:   C is best for dedicated workspace; B is next; A and D are more compact.
Final Pick for Your Priorities

Choose B: Campo de Ourique   if you want the safest overall match for your stated priorities in the order given. It is the only option that cleanly balances   budget, commute, quietness, light, and livability   without a major miss.
Choose A: Arroios   if you value a faster commute and a bit more budget breathing room, and you can tolerate some street noise.
Decision Notes for September 2026
Based on your criteria, I would use this shortlist logic:
-   Best overall:   B
-   Best value:   A
-   Best space:   C
-   Best if budget becomes flexible:   D
